title: 213. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Exponential Equations with Equal Bases
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve a basic exponential equation by expressing both sides with the same base.
questions.question: Solve \(2^x=8\).
questions.explanation: Write both sides with base \(2\). Since \(8=2^3\), the equation becomes \(2^x=2^3\). When the bases are equal, the exponents must be equal, so \(x=3\).
questions.hint: Express \(8\) as a power of \(2\), then equate the exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation by rewriting both sides with the same base.
questions.question: Solve \(3^{x-1}=27\).
questions.explanation: Write \(27\) as a power of \(3\): \(27=3^3\). The equation becomes \(3^{x-1}=3^3\). Since the bases are equal, \(x-1=3\), so \(x=4\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(27\) as \(3^3\), then equate the exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation by matching bases and solving the resulting linear equation.
questions.question: Solve \(5^{2x-1}=125\).
questions.explanation: Write \(125\) as a power of \(5\): \(125=5^3\). The equation becomes \(5^{2x-1}=5^3\). Equating exponents gives \(2x-1=3\), so \(2x=4\) and \(x=2\).
questions.hint: Express \(125\) as a power of \(5\), then set the exponents equal.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation by converting both sides to a common base.
questions.question: Solve \(4^x=8\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(4\) and \(8\) as powers of \(2\), then equate the exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation by expressing both sides as powers of the same base.
questions.question: Solve \(9^{x+1}=27^{x-1}\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(9\) and \(27\) as powers of \(3\), then equate the exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation where the exponents form a quadratic equation.
questions.question: Solve \(2^{x^2}=4^{x+3}\).
questions.explanation:
Write \(4^{x+3}\) with base \(2\): \(4^{x+3}=(2^2)^{x+3}=2^{2x+6}\). The equation becomes \(2^{x^2}=2^{2x+6}\), so \(x^2=2x+6\). Rearranging gives \(x^2-2x-6=0\). By the quadratic formula,
\[
x=\frac{2\pm\sqrt{4+24}}{2}=\frac{2\pm\sqrt{28}}{2}=1\pm\sqrt{7}
\]
questions.hint: Rewrite \(4\) as \(2^2\), then solve the resulting quadratic equation in the exponent.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation by converting both sides to base \(2\) and solving the linear equation.
questions.question: Solve \(2^{x+1}=8^{x-2}\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(8\) as \(2^3\), then equate the exponents and solve.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation by expressing both sides as powers of \(3\).
questions.question: Solve \(27^x=9^{x+1}\).
questions.explanation: Write both sides with base \(3\). Since \(27=3^3\), \(27^x=3^{3x}\). Since \(9=3^2\), \(9^{x+1}=3^{2(x+1)}=3^{2x+2}\). Equating exponents gives \(3x=2x+2\), so \(x=2\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(27\) and \(9\) as powers of \(3\), then equate the exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation by converting both sides to base \(2\) and solving for \(x\).
questions.question: Solve \(8^{x-1}=4^{x+2}\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(8\) and \(4\) as powers of \(2\), then set the exponents equal.

questions.concept: Solving exponential equations with equal bases
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential equation where the exponents form a quadratic equation with irrational solutions.
questions.question: Solve \(5^{x^2-1}=25^x\).
questions.explanation:
Write \(25^x\) with base \(5\): \(25^x=(5^2)^x=5^{2x}\). The equation becomes \(5^{x^2-1}=5^{2x}\), so \(x^2-1=2x\). Rearranging gives \(x^2-2x-1=0\). By the quadratic formula,
\[
x=\frac{2\pm\sqrt{4+4}}{2}=\frac{2\pm\sqrt{8}}{2}=1\pm\sqrt{2}
\]
questions.hint: Rewrite \(25\) as \(5^2\), then solve the resulting quadratic equation in the exponent.
